analysis.title: Equity Reverse Convertible Model Portfolios
key_insights: UBS CIO publishes model portfolios of equity reverse convertibles (RCs) for USD, EUR and CHF, built with its CIO RC methodology. The focus is six-month tenors.
RCs are pitched for two uses: earning extra income while waiting to buy a stock at a lower level ("buy on dip"), and generating yield in equity markets.
Single stock implied volatility has risen recently as markets assess the durability of the AI capex cycle. Higher implied volatility raises the coupon an RC can pay.

Each currency portfolio holds ten stocks, equally weighted, with a maximum 30% exposure to any one sector. Stocks must be 'CIO Selected' or rated 'Buy' by UBS Investment Bank. Swiss franc portfolios also admit 'Neutral' rated stocks because the universe is smaller.

The CIO methodology combines market data (implied volatility, momentum) with fundamentals (leverage, valuation ratios). It favors stocks with relatively higher implied volatility but lower risk metrics than peers. Stocks with too little implied volatility to deliver a minimum coupon are excluded.

UBS says the CIO methodology has performed well over the past 10 years and better than benchmark approaches such as picking the stocks with the highest implied volatility. Figure 1 shows higher CIO scores are associated with higher put writing returns across 3-, 6- and 12-month tenors, solving for a 10% p.a. option premium.

CIO worst-of baskets are used to raise yield, especially in low-yielding base currencies such as CHF and EUR or in defensive, low volatility sectors. The method excludes the bottom 25% to 40% of stocks by score, builds baskets of three (minimum two) top-scoring stocks in the same business area, and ranks baskets by overall score. Basket pricing includes a 2% p.a. distribution fee.

Payoff mechanics: at maturity, if the underlying is at or above the strike, the investor receives the invested capital back plus the coupon. If it is below the strike, the investor receives the stock physically or its cash value. The coupon pays for the downside exposure and for giving up upside above the strike.
Risks listed are loss of invested capital, limited secondary market liquidity, issuer default risk, and returns capped at the coupon with no dividends or appreciation.

Effective 1 November 2026, UBS CIO no longer rates or ranks equities in the Most Preferred, Bellwether and Least Preferred framework or publishes top picks. It now labels stocks 'CIO Selected', which is a designation and not a rating, and emphasizes portfolio-level analysis through CIO Equity Portfolios.

trade_ideas.description: Buy six-month reverse convertible model portfolios (ten equally weighted stocks each) in USD, EUR and CHF
trade_ideas.rationale: Reverse convertibles let investors earn yield while waiting to buy stocks at lower levels, and higher implied volatility lifts coupons.
trade_ideas.risk: Loss of invested capital if the stock ends below the strike, limited liquidity, issuer default risk, and returns capped at the coupon.

trade_ideas.description: Three best-scoring CIO worst-of reverse convertible baskets (starred in the report tables), built from sector Equity Preference Lists
trade_ideas.rationale: Worst-of baskets raise yield in low-yielding currencies or defensive, low volatility sectors where single stocks pay too little.
trade_ideas.risk: The basket pays out on the worst performer, so a breach by any one stock below the strike at expiry causes a loss.

risk_factors: Loss of invested capital if the underlying falls significantly below the strike at expiry.
Limited secondary market liquidity, so investors should be prepared to hold to maturity.
Limited return potential: capped at the coupon, with dividends and appreciation forgone.
Demand and supply for protection (volatility) may change over time and affect return characteristics.
Recent rise in single stock implied volatility tied to uncertainty over the durability of the AI capex cycle.
vol_and_positioning: Single stock implied volatility has risen recently as markets assess the durability of the AI capex cycle.

The report's RC pricing tables measure implied volatility percentile (six-month at-the-money implied volatility against its past one-year range) and richness (implied volatility minus realized volatility over the past year). The figures themselves are not in the extracted text.
Reverse convertibles are described as a way to sell volatility, since higher volatility produces higher coupons.
cross_bank_references: Stocks must be rated 'Buy' by UBS Investment Bank (or CIO Selected) to enter the portfolios. UBS CIO GWM says it has no influence on UBS IB ratings.

theme_stances.evidence: best risk-return trade-off for reverse convertibles
